ark-encounter.chronic.1.quote: A service animal relief area is located on-site beside Emzara’s Buffet. See our Accessibility Map for the location. Please note that “comfort,” “therapy,” and “emotional support” animals do not meet the definition of a service animal and are not permitted. Additionally, pets are not permitted at the Ark Encounter. Dietary When dining out, we understand how difficult choices can be when trying to avoid certain ingredients, whether it is due to food intolerances, food allergies , or personal choice. We offer both vegetarian and gluten-free options at Emzara’s Buffet. Please visit our Allergen Friendly Information pages for details. And if you have any questions regarding dietary needs during your visit, please request to speak with a restaurant manager—we would be glad to assist you! Deaf and Hard of Hearing Answers.TV Our streaming service, Answers.TV , is a wonderful resource with hundreds of captioned options! ASL Interpreter for Live Programs ASL interpreters are available for select daily programs on certain days. To view list of dates when ASL interpreters are scheduled, please click here . Deaf Days During our annual Deaf Days event , ASL interpreters and Deaf volunteers are available throughout the attraction to answer questions, assist with ticket purchases, interpret the shows and lectures and more! Exhibits The Ark Encounter exhibits are very visual and as you walk through them, you will find many video screens with open-captioned, short, educational videos. Much of the audio content in the Ark is available visually in the exhibits. Store The AnswersBookstore lists a variety of DVDs with captioning and subtitles. Theaters Videos and theaters in the Ark Encounter are almost all captioned. Virtually all videos playing in the Answers Center are captioned or can be upon request. Mobility The Ark Encounter attraction is fully wheelchair and stroller accessible. Ararat Ridge Zoo & Children’s Zoo All of the zoo’s pens are fully viewable via paved trails. The Children’s Zoo pathways are gravel. Carousel The deck of this carousel is set flush with the floor and includes a wheelchair securement system for manual wheelchairs. The carousel cannot accommodate motorized wheelchairs. Manual wheelchairs are available if a guest would like to transfer. Entrances Ramps are located at every entrance and exit door to Ark Encounter. The first entrance features an automatic door. Exhibit Access Virtually every exhibit is wheelchair accessible. A series of gradual ramps takes visitors through Ark Encounter’s main exhibits. An elevator is also available for access between floors. Parking We have many accessible parking spaces available in our main parking lot. If you need assistance finding an available space, alert the individual directing traffic. Restrooms All restrooms throughout the facility and grounds are accessible. Wheelchair accessible water fountains are also available near the main interior restrooms. For more information on adult changing tables, please talk to a team member at the Guest Services desk inside the Welcome Center.

ark-encounter.sensory.2.quote: There are no flashing or strobe lights inside the Ark. Upon entrance to the exhibits, there is one space created for experiencing what the flood might have been like while onboard the ark. This is a very loud area, complete with thunder sound effects and animal scratching and screeching noises in cages directly beside the guest walkway. If you have concerns about sensory overload here, it is possible to enter the exhibits via the elevator in the ground level Gift Shop. Once you have entered Deck 1, simply turn left to go back toward the beginning of the exhibits. This will allow you to bypass the loud area completely.

Virtual Reality Experience The Truth Traveler is a 4K virtual reality theater designed to take guests back in time to the days of the biblical Noah to see the building of the ark, the animals loading, and the floodwaters. The virtual reality experience is accessible. Please see more information here . Strollers, Wheelchairs, Wagons and ECVs The Ark is wheelchair- and stroller-friendly. You may bring your own or rent them upon arrival. Strollers, wheelchairs, and ECVs are available at Chariots of Tyre, located in the Welcome Center. When entering from the bus drop-off, it will be on your right, just past the Guest Services desk. Single strollers are available for a $15 fee. Wagons are available for a $20 fee. Manual wheelchairs are available for a $15 fee. A limited number of Electric Convenience Vehicles (ECVs) are available for a $45 fee. Rental fees are nonrefundable. See liability release and disclaimer notice . Sensory Christmas at the Ark Encounter Please be advised that there are flashing and quickly changing lights during the laser-light show projected onto the side of the Ark. Those with sensory sensitivities are advised to take appropriate precautions. Crowds and Sensory Overload The Ark Encounter serves thousands of guests each day. Crowds can be congested in the Ark exhibits. Take a break at any time from the exhibits by exiting via the elevator. ( See map. ) The expansive grounds and gardens, Ararat Ridge Zoo, the playground, and the carousel can be great ways to relax farther away from other guests. You can also plan to arrive at the Ark in the early afternoon to avoid the morning rush, as well as choose to first visit the grounds and zoo, the Answers Center theater and programs (found on your daily schedule), the playground, or the virtual reality show, as most guests will begin with the Ark exhibits. If you purchase a meal while on-site, try to go before noon or in the early afternoon to avoid lunch crowds. Exhibit Information The Ark Encounter exhibits are a visual experience with many signs, videos, and displays. There are no flashing or strobe lights inside the Ark. Upon entrance to the exhibits, there is one space created for experiencing what the flood might have been like while onboard the ark. This is a very loud area, complete with thunder sound effects and animal scratching and screeching noises in cages directly beside the guest walkway. If you have concerns about sensory overload here, it is possible to enter the exhibits via the elevator in the ground level Gift Shop. Once you have entered Deck 1, simply turn left to go back toward the beginning of the exhibits. This will allow you to bypass the loud area completely. Additionally, an exhibit titled, “Kid’s Spooky Animal Encounters” on Deck 2 is a children’s exhibit designed to experience being on the ark at night with animals on board. There are puffs of air in this exhibit, as well as background animal sounds, mirrors in the walls, and a jump-scare spot where a growling jaguar lights up in the dark. See more information in our Accessibility Map . Sensory Kits, Noise-Reducing Earmuffs and Earplugs For guests with sensory sensitivities, complimentary sensory kits, as well as noise-reducing earmuffs and earplugs, are available. Earmuffs and earplugs can be accessed at the admissions building upon arrival and at the Welcome Center Guest Services Desk. Sensory kits can be accessed at the Welcome Center Guest Services Desk. Simply provide the Ark team with your name and phone number to utilize these options during your visit. All items can be returned to the Welcome Center Guest Services desk before boarding the bus for your departure. (Note: Reservation of these options is not necessary.) Virtual Reality Experience The Truth Traveler is a 4K virtual reality theater designed to take guests back in time to the days of the biblical Noah to see the building of the ark, the animals loading, and the flood waters—all from a comfortable seat. This theater is much like a ride, and guests should be aware of this safety advisory before attempting. Strollers, Wheelchairs, Wagons and ECVs The Ark is wheelchair- and stroller-friendly. You may bring your own or rent them upon arrival. Strollers, wheelchairs, and ECVs are available at Chariots of Tyre, located in the Welcome Center. When entering from the bus drop-off, it will be on your right, just past the Guest Services desk. Single strollers are available for a $15 fee. Wagons are available for a $20 fee. Manual wheelchairs are available for a $15 fee. A limited number of Electric Convenience Vehicles (ECVs) are available for a $45 fee. Rental fees are nonrefundable. See liability release and disclaimer notice . Visual Audio Tours The Ark Encounter is pleased to offer a descriptive audio tour for the main exhibits. Guests can listen on their own devices. Learn more Braille Readers We are pleased to offer BRF files for portable braille readers. The content includes signage from each teaching deck inside the Ark Encounter. Click here to download and use these files for your braille reader . Braille Books Braille books are available on each of the three decks of the Ark, and include the text from the exhibits signs. Simply ask a Guest Services staff member for assistance upon reaching each deck.

aronoff-center-for-the-arts.chronic.1.quote: All restrooms in the Aronoff Center are accessible to people with disabilities. Restrooms in the Procter & Gamble Hall are located in the side corridors on both sides of the lobbies (except Balcony – restrooms located on the north side of the lobby only). Restrooms in the Jarson-Kaplan Theater and the Fifth Third Bank Theater are both one level below the theater and are accessible by elevator. A gender-neutral companion care restroom is located on the north side of the Loge lobby for guests requiring complete privacy or the assistance of a companion/parent. Please ask an usher or staff member for access.

aronoff-center-for-the-arts.chronic.2.quote: Service animals are always welcome and should remain on a leash or in a harness at all times. If you plan to bring a service animal to an event, please notify a representative at the time of purchase. Lactation Suite The TriHealth Lactation Suite is located inside the house left orchestra women’s restroom. The suite features a private area with comfortable seats, a changing station, dimmable lights, and outlets. Moms won’t need to worry about missing any of the action on the stage as the suite also contains a monitor feed of the stage.

aronoff-center-for-the-arts.chronic.3.quote: Restrooms in the Procter & Gamble Hall are located in the side corridors on both sides of the lobbies (except Balcony – restrooms located on the north side of the lobby only).

aronoff-center-for-the-arts.cognitive.1.quote: Designated rideshare drop-off and pick-up locations are on Walnut Street between 6th and 7th Streets. Directions The Aronoff Center is located one block north of Fountain Square in the heart of downtown Cincinnati and is easily accessible from surrounding expressways. For events in our Fifth Third Bank Theater, enter at the corner of 7 th and Main Streets. Construction Alert: The West side of downtown is currently experiencing ever-changing and expanding road construction and exit/street/highway closures due to the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor and Linn Street Reconstruction Projects. We strongly recommend using navigation apps for the most up-to-date directions. For project details, visit the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor website . From the North (I-75) Proceed south on I-75, take the Seventh Street exit east, proceed down Seventh Street to Walnut Street (about five blocks). From the North (I-71) Proceed south on I-71, take the Gilbert exit. Gilbert will become Eighth Street. Follow Eighth Street to Walnut Street. From the South (I-71 / I-75) Proceed north on I-71 / I-75 and follow signs across the river. Take the Fifth Street exit . Turn left on Vine Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street. From the South (I-471) Follow I-471 north over the bridge, take the Sixth Street exit and proceed down Sixth Street about five blocks; turn right on Vine Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street. Columbia Parkway (U.S. 50) Westbound on U.S. 50 : Take the Sixth Street exit and proceed down Sixth Street about five blocks; turn right on Vine Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street. Eastbound on U.S. 50 : Take the Fifth Street exit. Turn left on Elm Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street (about three blocks). Cincinnati Bell Connector (Streetcar) Running up to 18 hours a day and 365 days a year, the Cincinnati Bell Connector is an electric mode of transportation operating on a 3.6-mile loop connecting key communities in the city's urban core, from the riverfront to Findlay Market. Use the Aronoff Center Station at the corner of Seventh and Walnut Streets. For more information, visit our Cincinnati Bell Connector info page . Parking The Aronoff Center for the Arts is situated in the urban core of downtown Cincinnati. With more than 6,000 parking spaces within a two-block radius, there are a variety of parking options for guests attending performances at the Aronoff Center. Independently operated valet parking is available for most evening performances at establishments adjacent to the Aronoff Center on Sixth Street and Walnut Street. Guests attending performances are also encouraged to use the Aronoff Center’s designated drop-off and pick-up zone located on the south side of Seventh Street between Walnut and Main Streets. This location provides quick and easy access to the venue through the Aronoff’s North Plaza and Weston Art Gallery entrances. The Gallery entrance is handicap accessible and leads to an elevator that stops on all levels of the Procter & Gamble Hall.

aronoff-center-for-the-arts.mobility.1.quote: Accessible seating is available in all theaters for patrons not able to transfer out of their wheelchairs or with other seating needs. Please contact the Ticket Office at (513) 621-2787 in advance to discuss your needs. For accessible seating in the Procter & Gamble Hall, enter the building at street level. Take either elevator to: Level 3 for Orchestra seating, Orchestra Box B, and Loge Box E Level 4 for Loge seating and Balcony Box C & F Level 5 for Balcony seating

aronoff-center-for-the-arts.mobility.2.quote: A courtesy wheelchair is available upon request on a first-come, first-served basis for patrons needing assistance from the lobby to their seats. Patrons can ask any staff member or volunteer usher for assistance.

aronoff-center-for-the-arts.mobility.3.quote: The Jarson-Kaplan Theater and the Fifth Third Bank Theater are each equipped with one elevator for patron use. For the Procter & Gamble Hall, automatic accessible doors are located at the Weston Art Gallery entrance on the plaza near Seventh and Walnut Streets. For the Jarson-Kaplan Theater, automatic accessible doors are located on the south end of the building near Sixth and Walnut Streets. For access to the Fifth Third Bank Theater (at the corner of Seventh and Main Streets), there is a dedicated ramp on the south end of the entrance.

aronoff-center-for-the-arts.mobility.4.quote: For the Procter & Gamble Hall, two elevators are available for patron use, one in the Weston Art Gallery and one near the Aronoff Center Ticket Office. The Jarson-Kaplan Theater and the Fifth Third Bank Theater are each equipped with one elevator for patron use. For the Procter & Gamble Hall, automatic accessible doors are located at the Weston Art Gallery entrance on the plaza near Seventh and Walnut Streets. For the Jarson-Kaplan Theater, automatic accessible doors are located on the south end of the building near Sixth and Walnut Streets. For access to the Fifth Third Bank Theater (at the corner of Seventh and Main Streets), there is a dedicated ramp on the south end of the entrance.

aronoff-center-for-the-arts.mobility.5.quote: Please notify a representative at the time of purchase to request accessibility accommodations. Information and Accessibility Requests Ticket Office: (513) 621-2787 [ARTS] Administrative Office: (513) 721-3344 Email: ticketing@cincinnatiarts.org Access All theaters and meeting spaces within the Aronoff Center, including the Weston Art Gallery, are accessible to patrons with physical disabilities. Once inside the building, all levels are accessible by elevator. For the Procter & Gamble Hall, two elevators are available for patron use, one in the Weston Art Gallery and one near the Aronoff Center Ticket Office. The Jarson-Kaplan Theater and the Fifth Third Bank Theater are each equipped with one elevator for patron use. For the Procter & Gamble Hall, automatic accessible doors are located at the Weston Art Gallery entrance on the plaza near Seventh and Walnut Streets. For the Jarson-Kaplan Theater, automatic accessible doors are located on the south end of the building near Sixth and Walnut Streets. For access to the Fifth Third Bank Theater (at the corner of Seventh and Main Streets), there is a dedicated ramp on the south end of the entrance. Restrooms All restrooms in the Aronoff Center are accessible to people with disabilities. Restrooms in the Procter & Gamble Hall are located in the side corridors on both sides of the lobbies (except Balcony – restrooms located on the north side of the lobby only). Restrooms in the Jarson-Kaplan Theater and the Fifth Third Bank Theater are both one level below the theater and are accessible by elevator. A gender-neutral companion care restroom is located on the north side of the Loge lobby for guests requiring complete privacy or the assistance of a companion/parent. Please ask an usher or staff member for access. Assistive Listening Devices Assistive Listening Devices, designed to enhance the sound of performances for guests who are deaf or hard of hearing, are available at the Guest Services Desk, located in the southwest lower level of the Aronoff Center's Procter & Gamble Hall lobby, near the Ticket Office. This new system uses Listen Technologies' next generation of personal listening devices, and its integrated neck loop/lanyard improves the listening experience for T-coil users. Learn how to use the Assistive Listening Devices (ALDs) available at the Guest Services desk in the Procter & Gamble Hall Marble Lobby. Audio Description Audio description is a live narration of the visual aspects of the performance broadcast to visually impaired guests who wear a small receiver (headset). This narration includes pre-show descriptions of the theater and other important aspects of the performance, such as actions, sets, costumes, performers’ body language, and more. To request an audio-described performance, contact us at (513) 977-4157 or ticketing@cincinnatiarts.org . To ensure that we can accommodate your request, please contact us at least three weeks prior to the performance date. American Sign Language During American Sign Language (ASL) performances, skilled theatrical Interpreters translate spoken words and/or sung lyrics into sign language to help guests understand the performance. The Interpreters work with a Deaf ASL Consultant to translate the production into American Sign Language. The audience can see both the Interpreters and the stage action simultaneously from a designated area of the performance space. To request an ASL performance, contact us at (513) 977-4157 or ticketing@cincinnatiarts.org . To ensure that we can accommodate your request, please contact us at least three weeks prior to the performance date. Wheelchairs A courtesy wheelchair is available upon request on a first-come, first-served basis for patrons needing assistance from the lobby to their seats. Patrons can ask any staff member or volunteer usher for assistance. Accessible Seating Accessible seating is available in all theaters for patrons not able to transfer out of their wheelchairs or with other seating needs. Please contact the Ticket Office at (513) 621-2787 in advance to discuss your needs. For accessible seating in the Procter & Gamble Hall, enter the building at street level. Take either elevator to: Level 3 for Orchestra seating, Orchestra Box B, and Loge Box E Level 4 for Loge seating and Balcony Box C & F Level 5 for Balcony seating Service Animals Service animals are always welcome and should remain on a leash or in a harness at all times. If you plan to bring a service animal to an event, please notify a representative at the time of purchase.

ATTENDANTS & SERVICE ANIMALS Personal Care Attendants Policy Visitors who require paid Personal Care Attendants (PCA) may be accompanied by them at no additional cost during their visit to Newport Aquarium. This applies to general admission, group admission, membership, complimentary tickets and tickets purchased through third-party retail partners. Visitors who wish to purchase advance tickets should contact 1-800-406-3474 to request complimentary companion tickets for a paid PCA. These tickets must be picked up in person by the visitor and the paid PCA at the ticket window. Proper documentation of PCA status is required. For groups visiting with members having disabilities, we offer free admission for Personal Care Attendants (PCA). Groups can book in advance by calling 859-815-1478 . Service Animal Policy We only allow working Service Animals, in accordance with the American with Disabilities Act (ADA). Under the ADA, 'Service animals are defined as dogs that are individually trained to work or perform tasks for assisting people with disabilities. Newport Aquarium reserves the right to ask 2 questions: Is the dog a service animal required because of a disability? What work or task has the dog been trained to perform? Service animals must be harnessed, leashed or tethered unless these devices interfere with the service animal’s work or the individual’s disability prevents the use of these devices. In that case, the individual must maintain control of the animal through voice, signal or other effective controls. For the health and safety of your animal and yours, service animals are restricted from Penguin Encounters. Newport Aquarium does not offer a relief area for service animals. To leave the building and return, please be sure to bring your ticket with you. All animals must be well behaved and will need to leave the area if the handler is not able to enact proper control. Emotional Support / Comfort Animal Policy Dogs whose sole function is to provide comfort or emotional support do not qualify as service animals under the ADA. Pets, comfort animals, emotional support or therapy animals are not permitted at Newport Aquarium. Training of Service Animals Service animals that are being trained are permitted in Newport Aquarium. Trainers should be able to present documentation showing that they are professional trainers.
